cards.front: What is the relationship between an index and a record in the Lumen archive?
cards.back: An index maps a search key to the location of a stored record. A record contains the actual stored fields. An index can locate a record without containing all of that record's fields.
cards.locator: part 1 · Lumen archive › Index and record

cards.front: How does a stable key function when a record moves to a different storage location?
cards.back: A stable key keeps its value when a record moves to another storage location. A physical address can change when the record moves.

cards.front: How does the Lumen archive resolve a collision between two distinct keys?
cards.back: A collision occurs when two distinct keys map to the same index slot. The Lumen archive resolves a collision by storing the colliding records in a linked chain at that slot.

cards.front: What happens to the stored record fields when an index is rebuilt?
cards.back: Rebuilding an index recalculates the mapping from keys to locations. It does not change the stored record fields.

cards.front: When should you calibrate the fictional Mora instrument based on the chamber temperature?
cards.back: For the fictional Mora instrument, calibrate only when the chamber temperature is below 18 degrees Celsius. At exactly 18 degrees Celsius, postpone calibration.

cards.back: Collect a 12 mL sample after the indicator changes from amber to violet. Discard the first 2 mL; this discard is not part of the 12 mL collected sample.

cards.front: What does a successful indicator check confirm regarding the instrument's performance?
cards.back: A successful indicator check confirms that the indicator changed colour. It does not establish the measurement's accuracy. The note does not state the instrument's measurement accuracy.

cards.front: In the fictional Pebble queue, where does push(item) add an item?
cards.back: In this fictional queue, push(item) adds an item at the tail. pop() removes the item at the head.

cards.front: What does pop() return when called on an empty Pebble queue?
cards.back: Calling pop() on an empty Pebble queue returns None; it does not raise an exception.

cards.front: Why does the expression slots[2] read the third slot in the Pebble queue?
cards.back: The expression slots[2] reads the third slot because slot positions begin at zero. The literal sentinel is <empty>.

cards.front: What pointer does the supplied Pebble queue implementation store?
cards.back: The supplied implementation stores a tail pointer. push(item) updates that pointer and takes constant time. No timing claim is given for other implementations.
